subject: Aug 3 inference slowdown — post-incident summary and verification plan
messages:
From: Kathleen Chen <kathleen@acme-payments.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Aug 3 inference slowdown — request for postmortem and next steps

Hannah / Marissa,

Thanks for the incident update on Friday. The Aug 3rd degradation impacted a subset of our high-throughput endpoints for ~45 minutes and caused several orders to be delayed. Our on-call flagged higher tail latency and increased 5xx rates; engineering ran fallbacks but we'd like a formal postmortem (RCA, timeline, and corrective actions) to share with our SREs and compliance team.

Can you include:
- A brief root cause summary we can distribute to stakeholders
- Exact timeline of detection, mitigation, and closure
- Action items, owners, and expected completion dates
- Verification steps and who at Redwood will own the validation
- Any SLA credit or next steps for billing reconciliation (ticket SUP-4721)

We'd like the doc by EOD Friday (Aug 11) if possible. If not, an initial summary + a follow-up with attachments is fine. Also please include an engineer we can speak with about verification criteria.

Thanks,
Kathleen Chen
Head of Platform Reliability
Acme Payments

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Kathleen Chen <kathleen@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-11T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aug 3 inference slowdown — request for postmortem and next steps

Hi Kathleen — thanks for the note and apologies again for the disruption. Below is a concise RCA and proposed next steps; attached are a short digest (rca-digest.pdf) and event timeline (timeline.csv). I know your team needs something distributable — the digest is designed for that audience.

Executive summary (one paragraph):
On Aug 3 at ~10:13 PT, a partial serialization mismatch in our prefix/KV cache code exposed after a compatibility change in a kernel-level memory allocator led to cache misses under specific request patterns. The result was elevated model cold-starts and increased token-generation latency for a subset of customers during the 10:13–10:58 window. Automatic fallback behaved as designed but the fallback route experienced throttling due to a concurrent autoscaler lag, extending customer impact.

Key timeline (high level):
- 10:13 — anomalous latency spike detected by observability alert (internal metric: kv_cache_miss_rate)
- 10:17 — automated fallback triggered for affected routes
- 10:29 — autoscaler rate-limit reached on fallback pool, queuing increased requests
- 10:36 — engineering rollback of the allocator compatibility change initiated
- 10:41 — cache warm-up and KV invalidation completed, token latency returning toward baseline
- 10:58 — production graphs normalized; continued monitoring thereafter

Root cause: an interaction between a kernel allocator update and a serialization path in our prefix cache code that allowed a rare corruption state. The corruption increased miss rates and created a temporary surge in cold-starts.

Immediate remediations done during the incident:
- Rolled back the allocator change (owner: Platform Kernel Team)
- Scoped rate limits on fallback pool to prevent a single route from exhausting capacity
- Forced KV invalidation + targeted cache pre-population for impacted customers

Planned corrective actions (short to mid-term):
1) Patch and harden serialization guards (owner: Connor Obrien, eng) — targeted deploy: 2028-08-18
2) Autoscaler tuning and more aggressive fallbacks for transient cache blips (owner: Marissa Cole) — targeted deploy: 2028-08-22
3) Add preflight checks for allocator compatibility in our CI job (owner: Platform Kernel Team) — targeted deploy: 2028-09-01
4) Update runbooks and incident playbooks; add a post-incident verification checklist (owner: Hannah Schmitt) — targeted deliverable: 2028-08-20

Verification and acceptance criteria we propose:
- 99.9th percentile token latency for your high-throughput endpoints remains within 10% of baseline for a 24-hour continuous window
- Error rate (5xx) below 0.02% for the same verification window

We've attached the concise RCA and the raw timeline CSV; the full technical write-up is being finalized and will be added to the Drive link below. I've also opened SUP-4721 to coordinate SLA/billing reconciliation. Please confirm if the verification criteria above are acceptable and whether Aug 17 at 10:00 PT works for a 30–45 minute verification runbook walkthrough.

Attachments: rca-digest.pdf, timeline.csv
Related: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-4721

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kathleen Chen <kathleen@acme-payments.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-12T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aug 3 inference slowdown — request for postmortem and next steps

Kathleen — quick follow-up from Reliability: we confirmed the eligibility for an SLA credit under our policy; billing will calculate the amount once we have the confirmed impacted minutes (internal ticket SUP-4721).

On the technical side, Connor is our lead on the serialization guard patch and will own the canary rollout. I've attached a short canary plan (canary-plan.docx) that describes the staged rollout and rollback criteria. Summary of the plan:
- Canary phase 1: 1% of traffic on a dedicated canary pool for 4 hours; monitor kv_cache_miss_rate, 99.9p latency, and 5xx
- Canary phase 2: 10% traffic for 12 hours if phase 1 is stable
- Full roll if phase 2 meets acceptance criteria

Connor, can you join the Aug 17 verification call? We'll need an engineer in the meeting to approve the canary promotion.

Marissa Cole
VP, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Jonah Price <jonah@acme-payments.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kathleen Chen <kathleen@acme-payments.com>
Date: 2028-08-14T13:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aug 3 inference slowdown — request for postmortem and next steps

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the proposed verification criteria. Aug 17 at 10:00 PT works for us. A couple of notes from Acme's side:
- We agree to the verification acceptance thresholds Hannah proposed, with one addition: please include a 48-hour post-roll observation window after any full rollout before considering the mitigation complete
- Please circulate the canary-plan.docx and the final technical write-up at least 24 hours before the call
- We'll bring two SREs and one product owner to the meeting

Looking forward to the walkthrough.

Jonah Price
Senior SRE
Acme Payments

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Kathleen Chen <kathleen@acme-payments.com>, Jonah Price <jonah@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-16T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Final RCA summary, action owners, and verification schedule — Aug 3 incident

Kathleen / Jonah — attaching the finalized one-page RCA digest and the stabilized timeline (rca-digest.pdf, timeline.csv) and the canary plan (canary-plan.docx). Below is a consolidated action table and the meeting invite for Aug 17 at 10:00 PT.

Consolidated action items (owner — target date):
- Serialization guard patch (Connor Obrien) — 2028-08-18
- Canary rollout and monitoring dashboards (Marissa Cole) — start 2028-08-19; full rollout dependent on canary success
- Runbook updates and verification checklist (Hannah Schmitt) — 2028-08-20
- CI preflight allocator compatibility check (Platform Kernel Team) — 2028-09-01
- Billing/SLA reconciliation (Billing Ops, coordinated by Hannah) — initial calc by 2028-08-21

Meeting & verification: Aug 17, 2028 10:00 PT — 30–45 minute walkthrough; will cover canary phases, dashboards, and acceptance criteria. If the canary completes successfully, we will proceed with staged promotion and observe for 48 hours post full-roll as requested. Meeting link: https://meet.redwood.ai/acme-verification-0817

Acceptance criteria (final):
- 99.9th percentile token latency within 10% of baseline for 24 continuous hours during verification
- 5xx rate < 0.02% for the same window
- 48-hour post-roll observation period after full promotion

Please reply to this thread to confirm the meeting invite and the acceptance criteria. If you want Connor to run a short pre-call triage prior to Aug 17, he can make time on Aug 16 afternoon.

Thanks again for your patience. We own follow-through and will provide status updates in this thread and via SUP-4721.

Attachments: rca-digest.pdf, timeline.csv, canary-plan.docx
Links: https://drive.redwood.ai/share/ACME-RCA-2028-08, https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-4721

Best,
